title: Chapter 3 Quiz 5
description: Comparing values, combining conditions with AND, OR and NOT, and evaluating them.
instructions: Chapter 3: Comparison, logical operators and conditions.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: Match each comparison symbol to its meaning.
questions.explanation: These are the comparison operators of the course.

questions.question: What does the operator **<>** mean?
questions.explanation: <> tests that two values are different. Watch out: it is not 'less than or greater than' in one go.

questions.question: (5 > 3) AND (2 > 4) is True.
questions.explanation: AND needs both sides True. Watch out: 2 > 4 is False, so the whole condition is False.

questions.question: (5 > 3) OR (2 > 4) is True.
questions.explanation: OR needs only one side True, and 5 > 3 is True.

questions.question: NOT (3 = 3) is True.
questions.explanation: 3 = 3 is True, and NOT turns True into False. Watch out: NOT reverses the result.

questions.question: Which condition means 1 ≤ Index ≤ 10?
questions.explanation: Both limits must hold, and the limits themselves are included. Watch out: OR lets almost any number pass, and > or < would exclude 1 and 10.

questions.question: Let x = 4 and y = -2. Say whether each condition is True or False.
questions.explanation: x > 0 is True; x <> y is True; AND needs y > 0, which is False; OR is True because x > 0; NOT (x = y) is True. Watch out: y is negative.

questions.question: Let x = 0 and y = 0. Say whether each condition is True or False.
questions.explanation: With x = 0 and y = 0 all five conditions are False: x > 0 is False, x <> y is False, AND and OR are False, and NOT (x = y) is False because x = y. Watch out: zero is not greater than zero.

questions.question: Let x = 5. Which condition is **True**?
questions.explanation: x = 5 makes the second half of the first condition True. Watch out: x > 5 is False, but OR only needs one True side.

questions.question: This should display Pass when grade is from 10 to 20 (both included). One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Read(grade)
If (grade >= 10) OR (grade <= 20) Then
    Display("Pass")
EndIf
questions.explanation: Both limits must hold, so we need AND. Watch out: with OR every number passes, and the limit 10 must be included.

questions.assertion: (x > 0) OR (y > 0) is True when x = 3 and y = 0.
questions.reason: OR is True when at least one side is True.
questions.explanation: x > 0 is True, so the whole OR is True, which is what the rule says. Watch out: y > 0 is False, but it does not matter.
